title: Google Workspace + AI — Gemini in Gmail, Docs, Sheets & Slides

sections.content:
## What You'll Learn

If you use Google Workspace — Gmail, Google Docs, Sheets, Slides, or Drive — AI is now built directly into these tools. You don't need to switch between your work apps and a separate AI chat window. Gemini AI is embedded throughout the Google ecosystem, and in many cases you're already paying for it through your existing Google account or Workspace subscription.

By the end of this lesson you'll know exactly what AI is available in each Google app, what you need to access it, how to use it effectively in your real workflow, and the important differences between the free and paid tiers.

## What's Available and What It Costs

Google's AI features span several tiers — understanding which you have access to prevents frustration.

**Free (Google account required):**
- **Gemini.google.com** — the standalone Gemini chatbot (what we covered in lesson 2-4)
- **Google AI Studio** (aistudio.google.com) — free access to Gemini API for experimentation, no billing required
- **Smart Compose** in Gmail — AI-powered autocomplete suggestions (has existed since 2018)
- **Smart Reply** in Gmail — quick reply suggestions
- **Explore** in Sheets — basic chart suggestions and natural language queries (limited)

**Gemini for Google Workspace (paid add-on):**
- 'Help me write' in Gmail — full draft composition
- 'Help me write' in Docs — full document drafting and editing
- Gemini sidebar in Docs, Sheets, Slides — conversational AI panel
- 'Help me organise' in Sheets — AI-structured spreadsheets
- Speaker notes generation in Slides
- Gemini in Google Meet — meeting transcription and summaries

**Gemini Advanced (Google One AI Premium, $19.99/month):**
- Access to Gemini 2.5 Pro (the most capable model)
- Deep integration across all Workspace apps
- 1TB Google One storage included
- Access to Gemini in Gmail, Docs, Sheets, Slides simultaneously

**Business/Enterprise Workspace plans:**
- Gemini for Google Workspace Business Starter and above includes the paid Gemini features
- Your IT department may have already enabled these for your organisation

**The free-tier workaround:** Even without the paid Gemini Workspace add-on, you can:
1. Draft content in Gemini.google.com
2. Copy and paste into Gmail, Docs, or Sheets
This is slower but achieves the same result at no cost.

## Gemini in Gmail

Gmail is where many professionals spend a significant portion of their day. Gemini's Gmail integration targets the most time-consuming email tasks.

**Features available:**

**1. Help me write (paid tier)**
- Click the star/pen icon in the compose window → 'Help me write'
- Describe what you want: 'Write a professional decline to a vendor meeting request, keep it brief and friendly'
- Gemini writes the email → you can ask it to 'Formalise', 'Elaborate', 'Shorten', or 'I'm feeling lucky' for a random style variation
- Works in both new emails and replies

**2. Summarise this email (paid tier)**
- Open a long email thread → look for the 'Summarise this email' button at the top
- Gemini shows a bullet-point summary of the thread without you reading every email
- Particularly useful for catching up after leave or when assigned to an ongoing thread mid-conversation

**3. Gemini sidebar (paid tier)**
- The Gemini icon in the right panel opens a chat interface
- Ask questions about the email you're reading: 'What does this contract clause mean in plain English?'
- Ask it to help draft a response based on the thread: 'Draft a reply agreeing to the meeting but requesting an agenda first'
- Reference other Google content: 'Find the document Sarah sent me last week about the project budget'

**4. Smart Compose (free)**
- As you type, grey suggested text appears — press `Tab` to accept it
- AI-powered autocomplete based on your writing style and the email context
- Can be turned on/off in Gmail Settings → General → Smart Compose

**Best use cases:**
- Replying to complex threads where you need to understand context before responding
- Drafting difficult emails (declining requests, escalating issues, giving negative feedback)
- Catch-up summaries after time away
- Translating emails to/from other languages via the sidebar

## Gemini in Google Docs

Google Docs is where the Gemini integration is most mature and most useful for knowledge workers.

**Features available:**

**1. Help me write (paid tier)**
- Click the 'Help me write' prompt at the top of a new document, or `@Help me write` anywhere in a document
- Describe what you want created: 'Write a 500-word project proposal introduction for a website redesign project for a small retail business'
- Gemini drafts the content and inserts it into your document
- You can then ask for revisions: 'Make it shorter', 'Make it more formal', 'Add a section about timeline'

**2. Refine selected text**
- Select any text in your document → right-click → 'Help me write'
- Or select text and choose from: 'Rephrase', 'Summarise', 'Bulletise', 'Elaborate'
- This is a powerful editing tool: paste rough AI output or your own draft, then use Gemini to refine specific sections

**3. Gemini sidebar**
- The sidebar remains open while you work, letting you ask questions without leaving the document
- 'Summarise this document' — instant overview of a long document
- 'What are the key action items in this document?'
- 'Check this document for logical inconsistencies'
- 'Suggest a better structure for this document'
- '@Drive' — reference other documents: '@myQ3report.docx What were the revenue figures mentioned?'

**4. Generate images for your document (Gemini Advanced)**
- Prompt: 'Create an image of [description]' in the sidebar → inserts directly into the document

**Free-tier workflow:**
Without paid Gemini: open gemini.google.com in another tab → prompt for content → copy → paste into Docs → use Docs' built-in editing tools for formatting.

## Gemini in Google Sheets

Spreadsheets are powerful but intimidating for many users. Gemini in Sheets democratises data work.

**Features available:**

**1. Help me organise (paid tier)**
- Open a blank sheet or a sheet with some data → click 'Help me organise'
- Describe what you want: 'Create a content calendar template for social media, with columns for Date, Platform, Content Type, Caption, Image, Status'
- Gemini creates the structure with column headers and sample rows
- Useful for: project trackers, budgets, inventory lists, CRM tables, meeting logs

**2. Formula generation**
- Type `=` in a cell, then describe what you want in natural language
- 'Sum all values in column B where column A says "Confirmed"'
- Gemini suggests the correct formula (e.g., `=SUMIF(A:A,"Confirmed",B:B)`)
- This is available on free tiers in newer versions of Google Sheets

**3. Gemini sidebar for data analysis**
- Select a range of data → open Gemini sidebar → ask questions about it
- 'What is the average sale amount in this dataset?'
- 'Which product category has the highest return rate?'
- 'Identify any outliers in column C'
- 'Create a summary of this data in 3 bullet points'

**4. Chart creation (Explore feature — partially free)**
- In any sheet: click 'Explore' (bottom right) → ask natural language questions
- 'Create a chart showing monthly revenue by category'
- 'What's the trend in column D over time?'
- The Explore panel suggests charts and insights automatically

**The formula use case is the highest value for most users.** Google Sheets formulas are notoriously hard to remember. With Gemini, you describe what you want in plain English and get the correct formula — no Stack Overflow required.

## Gemini in Google Slides & Google AI Studio

**Gemini in Google Slides:**

**1. Help me create a presentation (paid tier)**
- In a new or existing presentation: click 'Help me create a presentation'
- Describe the presentation: 'Create a 10-slide presentation about the benefits of remote work for a business audience. Include a title slide, agenda, 7 content slides, and a closing slide with key takeaways.'
- Gemini creates the slide structure, content, and basic formatting
- You review, edit, and apply a professional theme

**2. Speaker notes generation**
- Select a slide → 'Help me write speaker notes'
- Gemini writes detailed speaker notes based on the slide content
- Saves time on presentation preparation, especially for content you'll present but not created yourself

**3. Image generation (Gemini Advanced)**
- Ask the sidebar to generate slide imagery: 'Create an image of a global team collaborating online for slide 3'
- Images are generated and can be inserted directly

**Google AI Studio (free, for experimentation):**

AI Studio (aistudio.google.com) is Google's free platform for experimenting with Gemini directly through the API. You don't need a paid plan — just a Google account.

Why use it:
- **Test Gemini's full capabilities** without the Workspace interface
- **Multimodal testing:** upload images, audio, video, and ask Gemini about them
- **System prompts:** write instructions that shape every conversation (same concept as Claude Projects or Custom GPTs)
- **Long context:** Gemini 2.5 Pro has a 1 million token context window — you can paste entire books or very long documents
- **Free API key:** AI Studio provides a free Gemini API key for developers (with usage limits)

**What to do in AI Studio:**
1. Go to aistudio.google.com → sign in
2. Click 'New prompt'
3. Try: upload a PDF and ask questions about it (tests the long-context capability)
4. Try: write a system prompt and see how it shapes responses
5. Try: use the 'Stream' option to see token-by-token generation

sections.title: Workshop A — Gmail AI: Summarise & Draft
sections.content:
You'll use Gemini's Gmail features (free workaround if you don't have paid tier, paid features if you do).

**If you have paid Gemini Workspace:**

**Step 1 — Summarise a long email thread:**
- Open any email thread with 5+ emails
- Look for the 'Summarise this email' button at the top of the thread
- Read the summary — how accurate is it? What did it miss?

**Step 2 — Draft a reply using Gemini:**
- In the reply box, click 'Help me write' (star icon)
- Type: 'Write a professional reply agreeing to a meeting but requesting an agenda be sent in advance'
- Review the draft, click 'Insert' to add it to your reply
- Edit the draft to personalise it, then send

**If you are using the free tier (workaround):**

**Step 1 — Copy the email thread content** (the full text of a long thread)

**Step 2 — Open Gemini.google.com** in another tab

**Step 3 — Paste the thread and ask:**
'Summarise this email thread in 3 bullet points and tell me what action I need to take: [paste thread]'

**Step 4 — For a reply draft, ask:**
'Based on this email thread, draft a professional reply that [your goal]. Keep it under 100 words and use a friendly but businesslike tone.'

**Step 5 — Copy the output** and paste it into your Gmail reply window. Edit as needed.

**For all users — try this challenge:**
Find an email in your inbox that you've been putting off because it requires a careful, diplomatic response. Use Gemini (either method) to draft it. Evaluate: did it capture the right tone and content? What did you need to edit?

**Outcome:** The email drafting workflow with AI — reducing the time and mental energy required for difficult correspondence.

sections.title: Workshop B — Google Docs: Write and Refine a Document
sections.content:
You'll use Gemini in Docs to create and refine a real document.

**Step 1 — Choose a document you need to write.** Pick something real:
- A meeting agenda
- A short report or update
- A policy or process document
- An email newsletter draft
- A project brief or summary

**If you have paid Gemini Docs:**

**Step 2 — Open a new Google Doc** and click 'Help me write'

**Step 3 — Describe your document:**
'Write a one-page [document type] for [audience] about [topic]. It should include: [list the key sections you need]. Tone: [professional/casual/formal]. Target length: [approx word count].'

**Step 4 — Review the draft** and use the refinement options:
- Select a section and choose 'Rephrase' to see alternative wording
- Select the summary paragraph and choose 'Elabor' to expand it
- Select a long section and choose 'Shorten' to make it more concise

**If you are using the free tier:**

**Step 2 — Write your document prompt in Gemini.google.com** (or Claude.ai)

**Step 3 — Copy the output** and paste into Google Docs

**Step 4 — Use Docs' built-in tools** for formatting: heading styles, table of contents, spell check

**For all users — try the sidebar (paid) or Gemini window (free):**
- 'Summarise this document in 3 bullets'
- 'What are the action items in this document?'
- 'Check this document for any logical inconsistencies'
- 'Suggest a better heading for section 2'

**Outcome:** A completed document draft in a fraction of the time, plus familiarity with the editing workflow.

sections.title: Workshop C — Google Sheets: Formulas & Structure
sections.content:
You'll use AI to do things in Google Sheets that previously required knowing specific formulas.

**Part 1 — Formula generation (available on some free tier versions):**

**Step 1 — Open a Google Sheet** with some data (or create one with test data: 5 names in column A, a number in column B, and a status like 'Paid' or 'Unpaid' in column C).

**Step 2 — In a blank cell, try asking for a formula** by describing what you want:
- Click an empty cell, type `=` then describe in natural language in the formula bar
- OR: open the Gemini sidebar and ask 'Write a formula to sum column B only where column C says Paid'
- Apply the suggested formula and test it

**Try these formula requests:**
- 'Find the average of column B'
- 'Count how many cells in column C say Unpaid'
- 'Look up a name in column A and return the value from column B in that row'
- 'Calculate what percentage of the total each row's value represents'

**Part 2 — Create a template (paid Gemini or free workaround):**

**If paid:** New sheet → 'Help me organise' → type: 'Create a personal budget tracker with income and expense categories, monthly columns for Jan-Dec, and totals'

**If free:** Ask Claude.ai: 'Create a Google Sheets template for [your use case]. List the column headers, suggested row structure, and 2-3 formulas I should know for this template.' Then build it manually in Sheets using the instructions.

**Part 3 — Explore panel:**
In any sheet with data: click 'Explore' (bottom-right compass icon)
- Ask natural language questions about your data
- Click on suggested charts to insert them
- Note which questions it answers well vs. where it struggles

**Outcome:** The ability to use Google Sheets for data work without needing to memorise formulas — AI handles the syntax, you handle the logic.

sections.title: Workshop D — Google Slides: AI Presentation
sections.content:
You'll create a presentation structure with AI — either using the paid Gemini Slides feature or the free workflow.

**Step 1 — Choose a presentation topic.** Use a real one you need to create:
- A project update for your team
- An explainer about a topic in your field
- A training or onboarding presentation
- A proposal or pitch
- Or use: 'Introduction to AI for a non-technical business audience'

**If you have paid Gemini in Slides:**

**Step 2 — New presentation → 'Help me create a presentation'**

**Step 3 — Describe your presentation:**
'Create a 10-slide presentation about [topic] for [audience]. Include a title slide, agenda, 7 content slides with key points and data where relevant, and a closing slide with key takeaways and next steps.'

**Step 4 — Review and refine:**
- Click on any slide → use the sidebar to 'Add more content to this slide'
- Select a slide → 'Help me write speaker notes' to get talking points
- Apply a professional theme from the 'Slide' menu → 'Change theme'

**If you are using the free tier:**

**Step 2 — Build the outline in Claude or Gemini.google.com:**
'Create a 10-slide presentation outline for [topic] for [audience]. For each slide, provide: slide title, 3-5 bullet points, and speaker note suggestions.'

**Step 3 — Copy the outline into Google Slides** and build each slide from the AI-generated content

**Step 4 — Apply a theme** from the template gallery and add images from Unsplash or AI-generated imagery

**For all users:**
Once you have a rough presentation, use this prompt in Gemini or Claude: 'Review this presentation outline. Is the narrative arc clear? Does each slide build logically on the last? What's missing? Is the content appropriate for a [audience description]?'

**Outcome:** A complete presentation created in under 30 minutes that would normally take 2-3 hours.

sections.title: Workshop E — Google AI Studio Exploration
sections.content:
Google AI Studio is free and lets you experiment with Gemini's most powerful capabilities — including the 1 million token context window.

**Step 1 — Go to aistudio.google.com** and sign in with your Google account.

**Step 2 — Create a new prompt** (click '+ New Prompt' or 'New stream prompt').

**Step 3 — Try the long context capability (this is Gemini's unique strength):**
- Find any long document you have: a report, a research paper, a contract, a book excerpt
- Upload it using the file/document icon (Gemini 2.5 Pro can handle 1 million tokens — roughly 700,000 words)
- Ask questions about it: 'Summarise the key findings', 'What are the action items?', 'Does this contradict anything else in the document?'

**Step 4 — Try multimodal input:**
- Upload a photo (your own, or any image)
- Ask: 'Describe what is in this image', 'What text can you see?', 'What mood does this image convey?'
- Upload a short video clip if you have one — Gemini can analyse video content

**Step 5 — Experiment with system prompts:**
- In the left panel, look for 'System instructions'
- Write: 'You are a professional editor. When I share writing with you, give feedback on structure, clarity, and tone. Always suggest 3 specific improvements.'
- Then paste some of your own writing and see how the system prompt shapes the feedback

**Step 6 — Get a free API key:**
- Click 'Get API key' in the AI Studio interface
- This API key lets you make programmatic calls to Gemini for free (with rate limits)
- Note: this is the same concept as the Anthropic API key you'll get in Part 17 (lesson 11-3)

**Outcome:** Familiarity with Gemini's full capabilities beyond the chat interface — especially the long context and multimodal features that distinguish it from Claude and ChatGPT.

sections.question: You need to summarise a 40-email Gmail thread before responding to it, but you only have a free Google account. What is the most practical approach?
options: Upgrade to Gemini Advanced to access the Gmail summary feature
Read all 40 emails to understand the thread
Copy the email thread text, open gemini.google.com or Claude.ai in another tab, paste the thread, and ask for a summary and recommended response
Wait and see if someone else summarises it in a reply
sections.explanation: Option C is the correct free-tier workaround. Copying email thread content and pasting it into a separate AI chat window achieves the same result as the native Gmail integration — it's just slightly more manual. Most long email threads are thousands of words, which fits easily within any modern AI's context window. Option A works but adds a recurring subscription cost for something achievable for free with an extra 30 seconds of effort. Option B defeats the purpose of using AI for this task.

sections.question: A colleague says 'I don't need to learn Excel or Sheets formulas anymore because AI writes them for me.' What is the most accurate response to this?
options: Correct — AI makes formula knowledge completely obsolete
Wrong — you should still memorise all formulas and ignore AI

Partially correct: AI is excellent at generating formulas from plain-English descriptions, which reduces the need to memorise syntax. However, you still need to understand what a formula does to verify it's correct, to troubleshoot when it doesn't work, and to decide which formula to ask for in the first place.
AI can only write simple formulas — for anything complex you still need expert knowledge
sections.explanation: Option C is the nuanced, accurate answer. AI dramatically reduces the need to memorise formula syntax — you describe what you want, AI provides the formula. But understanding the underlying logic remains important: you need to verify that the formula actually does what you think, notice when the AI misunderstood your request, and have enough understanding to debug errors. The practical implication: you need less memorisation but the same conceptual understanding of what formulas do.

sections.question: What is Google AI Studio's unique capability that distinguishes it from using Gemini.google.com or Gemini in Workspace?
options: It provides access to Gemini 2.5 Pro's 1 million token context window, multimodal inputs (images, video, audio), system prompt configuration, and a free Gemini API key — all free, without a paid Workspace subscription
It integrates directly with Gmail and Docs
It generates images better than other Gemini products
sections.explanation: Google AI Studio (option B) is the developer and experimentation platform that exposes Gemini's full capabilities for free. The 1 million token context window is Gemini's most distinctive technical capability — no other mainstream AI offers this at the same scale. The ability to analyse video and audio as inputs is also unique. And critically, AI Studio provides free API access with usage limits, making it the starting point for anyone wanting to build with the Gemini API. The Workspace integration (Gmail, Docs) requires a paid subscription — AI Studio's free access is the alternative entry point.

sections.content: **You've completed lesson 2-16.** You now know the full Google Workspace AI ecosystem: Gemini in Gmail for email drafting and thread summaries, Gemini in Docs for document creation and editing, Gemini in Sheets for formula generation and data questions, Gemini in Slides for presentation creation, and Google AI Studio for advanced experimentation. If you're a Google Workspace user, these tools are the path of least resistance — the AI is where the work already happens.
